newsitem.title: GERMANY: Grundig surprised by Philips share sale.
newsitem.headline: Grundig surprised by Philips share sale.

text.p: Germany's Grundig AG said on Friday it was surprised Philips Electronics NV would sell a huge chunk of its stake in the troubled home electronics maker to a London investment house.
Grundig's management board also said in a statement it disputed Philips' claim that the German company had inflated its 1996 loss after the end of the year.
"The board decidedly contradicts the view of Philips" that last year's 671 million mark loss was increased by restructuring charges taken in 1997, the company said.
It added that its 1996 results were approved by KPMG in Duesseldorf, an accounting firm chosen by Philips when the Dutch giant had management control of Grundig.

"For years KPMG has also been the auditing firm for Philips and took over the auditing of Grundig out of the express wishes of Philips in order to guarantee a unified accounting in the Philips concern," Grundig said.
Philips on Friday said it would go to court to have the Grundig's 1996 Annual Accounts nullified.

It also announced it would cut its share of Grundig to five percent by selling a 26.6 percent stake to Botts & Co Ltd. Botts also bought a 16.4 percent stake of Grundig shares held by German asset management first Hohenstaufen Vierundviertigste Vermoegensverwaltung GmbH.
After losing millions of marks on Grundig, Philips announced at the end of 1996 that it was giving up management control granted through a contract with the Grundig Foundation.
